heading: INT. MADAME ROUSSEL'S SALON - PARIS - EVENING (1791)

units.text: INT. MADAME ROUSSEL'S SALON - PARIS - EVENING (1791)
Candles in silver sconces.
Gilt chairs.
A harpsichord with its lid closed.
Six guests sit around a tea table, porcelain cups trembling on saucers, as the window shows a red dusk beyond the curtains.
MADAME ROUSSEL, 50s, presides in powdered hair.
Her husband, MONSIEUR ROUSSEL, 60s, studies the sugar tongs.
Their niece, LOUISE, 18, watches the window.
A young poet, ANTOINE, 20s, fiddles with a cravat pin.
A priest, ABBÉ FOURNIER, 60s, stirs his tea long past need.
An officer, CAPTAIN DUVALIER, 30s, sits stiffly, hand on his sword.
More sugar, Abbé?
units.name: MADAME ROUSSEL

units.text: No, Madame, I—
units.name: ABBÉ FOURNIER

units.text: Did you hear that?
units.name: LOUISE

units.text: It's only the carriage.
units.name: ANTOINE

units.text: At this hour there are no carriages.
units.name: MONSIEUR ROUSSEL

units.text: I will see.
units.name: CAPTAIN DUVALIER

units.text: Sit down, Captain.
units.name: MADAME ROUSSEL

units.text: Child, it is nothing.
units.name: ABBÉ FOURNIER

units.text: It is a drum.
units.name: LOUISE

units.text: Silence.
The tea steams.
Far below, a drumbeat rolls through the street.
Then, much closer, a fist on the front door.
Madame Roussel pours another cup with perfect, trembling grace.
